verdict.rationale: Discord's developer docs show two credential types—bot tokens and OAuth2 bearer tokens—with OAuth2 registration flow and scope-based access (e.g., only `/users/@me/connections` requires the connections scope), which supports issuing narrower, purpose-specific credentials than a full bot token. However, there's no explicit documentation of a permission/scope catalog, least-privilege guidance, or agent-specific credential issuance workflow. Missing for 10: explicit least-privilege/scope granularity documentation, guidance for issuing agent-specific restricted tokens, and independent confirmation of scope enforcement in practice.
